findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit request cancellation
findings.body: `WithTimeoutCause` derives the new context from the incoming request context; it does not detach it. When the API server finishes the request, cancellation propagates to this goroutine, potentially aborting the legacy write before the 10-second timeout. The same pattern is used for delete, update, and delete-collection, so successful unified writes may not be mirrored. Use a context that preserves needed values but is independent of request cancellation, then apply the timeout.

findings.title: Independent goroutines can reorder writes for the same object
findings.body: Each successful request launches an independent legacy-write goroutine, with no ordering or version guard. For example, an update can reach legacy before the earlier create and fail with NotFound; if the delayed create then succeeds, legacy is left stale. A delayed delete can likewise run after a recreate and remove the newer legacy object. Since these background errors are not returned to the caller, the divergence can persist. Serialize shadow writes per resource or otherwise ensure stale operations cannot overwrite newer ones.

findings.title: Legacy updates recompute the mutation against legacy state
findings.body: The legacy update receives the original `objInfo` instead of the result of the unified update. For patches or other updates whose result depends on the old object, `Legacy.Update` applies the mutation to the legacy copy's potentially divergent state and can produce a different object from unified storage. Pass the unified result through an updated-object wrapper or otherwise ensure the legacy write stores that same result.

findings.title: Unified NotFound now skips legacy deletion
findings.body: This returns for every unified delete error, including NotFound, without attempting the legacy delete. The previous mode-3 implementation specifically continued to legacy on unified NotFound, which lets a delete clean up a legacy-only orphan during migration or after divergence. Preserve that behavior while still returning the unified NotFound response, or explicitly handle orphan cleanup another way.

findings.title: Delete metrics use the object name as the kind label
findings.body: This passes `name` as the third argument to `recordStorageDuration`, while the other operations pass `options.Kind` for that label. If the metric uses this argument as its kind/resource label, every distinct object name creates a new Prometheus label value, causing unbounded cardinality and potentially exposing resource names. Pass the kind instead.

findings.title: Delete-collection shadow writes are recorded as storage metrics
findings.body: This records the duration and error of `Legacy.DeleteCollection` with `recordStorageDuration`, even though the unified-storage duration was already recorded at line 159. As a result, legacy delete-collection failures and latency are attributed to storage. Use the legacy recorder here; storage create and update failures are also currently attributed to legacy at lines 45 and 129.
